description: A strip of very thin leather worked into the inner hinge to face the joint where board meets textblock. It adds little strength but gives a refined finish to the inside of the board, and must be pared down so the board still closes properly.
name: leather joint

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1902), Chapter V, p.80. Internet Archive.
